newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Gazan industrialists protest at Israeli measures. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Gazan industrialists protest at Israeli measures. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]

text.p: Palestinian industrialists blocked a Gaza thoroughfare with machinery-laden trucks on Wednesday to protest against an Israeli economic blockade which has squeezed exports from the self-ruled enclave, Palestinians said.
Witnesses said some 200 Gazan factory owners crammed about 30 trucks bumper-to-bumper into a double line in front of the Palestinian Ministry of Industry, blocking traffic.
"We are protesting against Israeli treatment of our businesses and our goods," Naser al-Sarraj (corrects first name from Maser), director-general of the ministry, told reporters.
Sarraj said Israeli restrictions preventing Gazan factory owners from travelling to the West Bank had crippled business in autonomous Palestinian areas.
"We receive only 100 permits for 3,500 business owners to enter Israel," he said.

Industrialists said an Israeli closure of the West Bank and Gaza, imposed during a wave of Islamist suicide bombings which killed scores in the Jewish state last February and March, had severed Gazan goods from Palestinian markets in the West Bank.
"My main market is Gaza and the West Bank and since the closure I now export zero to the West Bank," said canned goods producer Rashad Hamada.
Hamada, whose Badr vegetable cannery is the largest in the Palestinian territories, said he had lost about $700,000 since the closure.
"I am employing 55 workers who are getting paid for doing nothing. I will lose lots of canned food if they don't make it to market before expiration," he told Reuters.
Israeli and Palestinian economic officials on Monday agreed to form a committee to discuss increasing the number of permits for Palestinian businessmen seeking to enter Israel.
"If the closure continues in this way, our economy will die," Sarraj said.
